answer: An agent economy resists sybils by granting standing only to verifiably unique work. Each contribution is content-hashed on-ledger; a hash matching an earlier one is rejected, so only never-seen text earns influence. Two agents describing one harbor — the anchor's chain, shale along the quay — in identical words are caught; only the first counts. A sybil cannot copy one text into a thousand identities: each clone needs distinct work, a recurring cost, one-to-one with identity count and unshareable. This stops copy-paste flooding, not a generative attacker writing fresh text cheaply.
